title: Varno River
text:
Varno River
[INFOBOX]
Length | 212 km
Source | Mount Hesk
Mouth | Gulf of Pell

The Varno River is a river in the province of Ardel. It rises on Mount Hesk and flows south into the Gulf of Pell.

## Course
From its source the river passes three towns, in this order:
- Tessby
- Orlin
- Calder Ford

Below Calder Ford the river widens into a marsh before it reaches the sea.

title: Tessby
text:
Tessby
[INFOBOX]
Province | Ardel
Founded | 1312
River | Varno River

Tessby is a market town on the upper Varno River. It was granted a charter in 1312.

## People
- Mira Halden (1871-1938), composer, was born in Tessby.

title: Orlin
text:
Orlin
[INFOBOX]
Province | Ardel
River | Varno River

Orlin is a town on the middle course of the Varno River. Its best-known landmark is the Orlin Bridge, a stone bridge over the river.

title: Calder Ford
text:
Calder Ford
[INFOBOX]
Province | Ardel
River | Varno River

Calder Ford is a village at the last crossing of the Varno River before the Gulf of Pell. The architect Joran Vesk was born here in 1840.

title: Mira Halden
text:
Mira Halden
[INFOBOX]
Born | 1871, Tessby
Died | 1938, Pell
Occupation | Composer

Mira Halden was a composer from Ardel. She grew up in her birthplace, Tessby, and later taught in the city of Pell.

## Works
- The Glass Orchard (opera, 1904)
- Songs of the Varno (song cycle, 1910)

title: The Glass Orchard
text:
The Glass Orchard
[INFOBOX]
Composer | Mira Halden
Premiere | 1904, Pell Royal Theatre

The Glass Orchard is an opera in three acts by Mira Halden. It was first performed in 1904 at the Pell Royal Theatre.

title: Pell Royal Theatre
text:
Pell Royal Theatre
[INFOBOX]
City | Pell
Opened | 1879
Architect | Joran Vesk

The Pell Royal Theatre is an opera house in the city of Pell. It was designed by Joran Vesk and opened in 1879.

title: Joran Vesk
text:
Joran Vesk
[INFOBOX]
Born | 1840, Calder Ford
Died | 1902
Occupation | Architect

Joran Vesk was an architect from Ardel.

## Buildings
- Pell Royal Theatre (1879)
- Orlin Bridge (1889)
